articles.title: US Open 2026 results: Elena Rybakina replaces Aryna Sabalenka as women's world number one with win over Zheng Qinwen
articles.summary: Elena Rybakina becomes the new women's world number one after reaching the US Open semi-finals, ending Aryna Sabalenka's 99-week reign at the top of the rankings.
articles.body:
After 99 weeks, there will be a new women's world number one - and it will be Elena Rybakina.

Rybakina confirmed she will replace Aryna Sabalenka at the top of the world rankings on Monday with her US Open quarter-final victory over China's Zheng Qinwen.

Despite losing a set for the first time in the tournament, Rybakina fought back and saved a break point in the deciding set to complete a 3-6 6-1 6-4 win.

She is the first Kazakhstani man or woman to reach the top of the singles standings.

Rybakina has been in hot pursuit of Sabalenka this season and arrived in New York as one of three women who threatened the Belarusian's position, alongside Americans Jessica Pegula and Coco Gauff.

However, the other three contenders each needed to win the title and hope Rybakina exited before the semi-finals to capture the number one spot.

Sabalenka's consecutive 99-week reign as world number one stretches back to 21 October 2024 and stands as the sixth-longest streak in WTA history.

The top two players could yet meet in the US Open final - just as they did at this year's Australian Open, where Rybakina prevailed in three sets.

For Rybakina, the trophy is more important than her new ranking.

"It's just a number right now. My goal is to win the tournaments which I play," the 27-year-old sad.

"It's an amazing achievement, but you know how quickly everything can change in tennis ranking-wise."

Rybakina will face either Coco Gauff or Mirra Andreeva in Thursday's semi-finals, while Sabalenka takes on Jessica Pegula.

Shelton beats Alcaraz in late-night 'war' to reach semis

Rybakina's push for the world number one ranking started at the end of 2025.

After losing to Sabalenka in the quarter-finals of the Wuhan Open last October, Rybakina clinched the Ningbo Open title one week later before taking her revenge by beating Sabalenka to win the season-ending WTA Finals.

She carried that momentum into 2026, getting the better of Sabalenka again but this time in a major final. She beat her fellow big-server in three competitive sets to win the Australian Open - her second Slam title almost four years after her first at Wimbledon.

Since then, Sabalenka has come out on top in their Indian Wells final and Miami Open semi-final, but Rybakina took the Stuttgart title on clay as Sabalenka's form fluctuated.

After disappointing early exits at the French Open and Wimbledon, she reached the final in Toronto, losing in straight sets to Iga Swiatek.

Rybakina's bid to replace Sabalenka suffered another setback when she was forced to retire injured from her Cincinnati Open quarter-final against Swiatek last month.

Rybakina later revealed that the left ankle problem, which hindered her movement and prevented her pushing off properly when serving, had been "bothering me for a long period of time" but was something she felt she had "under control".

Speaking before the US Open, Rybakina admitted her preparation "wasn't great" as she was unable to train for much of the week leading into the tournament.

However, that has not stopped her from achieving the first of her two major goals in New York.

How Rybakina asserted herself at the top

Rybakina's rise to world number one has coincided with one of the most consistent periods of her career.

Despite managing her ankle injury in the lead-up to the US Open, Rybakina has backed up a 78-match 2025 season by playing 60 times so far this year.

She has won 47 of those matches, a tally bettered only by American world number three Pegula (50) on the WTA Tour.

Only Pegula can match her tally of 34 wins on hard courts this season.

But Rybakina has also won the majority of her matches against the tour's other leading players, winning 13 of her 20 meetings with fellow top-20 players.

Undoubtedly Rybakina's biggest weapon is her powerful serve.

She has recorded the most aces on the WTA Tour this year, with her total standing at 394 in 2026.

Rybakina's serve was at its devastating best against Naomi Osaka in the fourth round - she won 87% of her first-serve points and fired in seven aces among her 29 winners, but limited her unforced errors to 17.

Speaking after the match, Osaka said: "The immediate thought that I had in my head when she hit the ace, I was, like, 'well, I can't really do anything about it'."

"Maybe I could have covered it, but she has a great serve, so she probably would have hit the other way."

Rybakina has worked with coach Stefano Vukov for almost seven years.

The pair first worked together from 2019 to 2025 before splitting. Later that year Vukov was banned from the WTA Tour for breaching its code of conduct, following an independent investigation into his behaviour towards Rybakina.

Vukov, who has coached Rybakina since she was a teenager, denied any wrongdoing, and Rybakina said she was never mistreated by him.

Rybakina sought his return to her team at the start of 2025. The Croat successfully appealed the suspension and began working with Rybakina again in August last year.

She reached the US Open fourth round for the first time in her career at her first tournament since reuniting with Vukov, before embarking on the strong end-of-season form which has now propelled her to the pinnacle of the sport.

articles.body: Naomi Osaka claims she doesn't care about what her critics think of her or her extravagant outfits, but she cares enough to call them out on social media. The four-time Grand Slam winner donned a number of different, very bold pre-match outfits throughout the U.S. Open, a trend she's set for many years at this point in her career. I don’t mind being the first to do something and getting trashed for it," Osaka wrote on Instagram Threads. "This happened when I talked about mental health and for some reason it’s happening with my clothes lol. I’m literally Haitian it’s in my blood to be this way, as long as the people after me have an easier path it’s worth it." THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Osaka was born in Osaka, Japan, and plays under the Japanese flag, but her father, Leonard Francois, is from Jacmel, Haiti, hence her nod to her line about having Haitian blood. She and her family moved from Japan to Long Island, New York, when she was three years old. Osaka kicked off her 2026 U.S. Open journey by wearing a short-sleeved hoodie, red and black arm sleeves, and a full-length skirt ahead of her first-round match. articles.title: US Open 2026: Coco Gauff mounts stunning comeback to set up Elena Rybakina semi-final
articles.summary: Coco Gauff saves match points in epic fightback to floor Mirra Andreeva; Gauff will face new world No 1 Elena Rybakina after she beat Qinwen Zheng to reach US Open semi-finals; watch the US Open live on Sky Sports Tennis
articles.body:
It was a horrible start for 2023 champion Gauff, whose serve and forehand deserted her as she lost the first set in just 26 minutes, hitting only three winners and making 14 unforced errors.

She improved in the second which culminated in a tie-break, during which Russian fifth seed Andreeva squandered two chances to take the match.

That broke Andreeva's spirit and she risked being defaulted after hurling her racket towards her chair, inadvertently sending it spinning towards a camera operator who had to dodge out of the way.

Gauff eventually won 2-6 7-6 (7) 6-2 and revealed she took inspiration from a fellow American's comeback on Tuesday.

"I just had to reset," Gauff said. "I came out at the start, not feeling the ball, giving her too many free points.

"Mirra was playing a great level, but when I went to the restroom after the first set, honestly I was thinking about Frances Tiafoe and how he came back yesterday.

"We all want to do well in front of this crowd. I was trying to leave the court with no regrets, I didn't know what outcome would come. You guys really helped pull me through."

'Gauff one of few capable of wins like that'

"That was just pure heart to find a way, somehow. It doesn't really matter the level, you just have to find a way on the day.

"She's the one tomorrow in the semi-final of the US Open. If she wins the US Open, no one will remember her level here in the quarters.

"Coco Gauff is one of the only players in the world capable of winning a match like that."

'Difficult defeat to get over for Andreeva'

"It was amazing to watch, because you've got two brilliant players capable of playing some amazing tennis who through serving issues and errors became so tight and so nervous.

"The ball speed deteriorated, and went down and down. But that's the beauty of tennis. It's about keeping the ball on the island and cutting out unforced errors.

"That is going to be a very difficult defeat for Andreeva to get over, having had match points in the second set. But she will learn so much from it. She'll be incredibly disappointed."

Rybakina claims world No 1 spot after Zheng battle

Earlier, Rybakina clinched the world No 1 spot after beating Qinwen Zheng to book her place in the last four.

The 27-year-old from Kazakhstan will usurp Aryna Sabalenka, whose 99-week reign at the top of the rankings will end on Monday.

Rybakina, the Australian Open champion, has been chasing down Sabalenka all year and will be No 1 for the first time in her career even if the Belarusian goes on to win a third consecutive title.

But Rybakina will have something to say about that as well, having reached the last four at Flushing Meadows for the first time.

"It's just a number right now, I'm only in the semis and the goal is to win every tournament I play," she said. "I feel like I just need to focus on my game and enjoy tomorrow."

Rybakina dropped a set for the first time this fortnight but hit back strongly in the second.

And Zheng's near-12 hours on court, through three qualifying matches and five in the main draw, finally caught up with her in the decider as Rybakina won 3-6 6-1 6-4.

"It's tough to find words," added Rybakina. "It was a very difficult match, lot's of nerves, maybe not the highest level but I'm glad I pushed through.

"I didn't start that well, I was too negative. It was a lot of unforced errors but I told myself to keep on fighting."

Zheng was enjoying an Emma Raducanu-style run in New York but, although the 23-year-old from China's fairytale eventually came to an end, she is now back on the verge of the top 50 having slipped to 121 after elbow surgery.

"It ended up being a really good performance.

"It wasn't the best start from Rybakina, Zheng had something to do with that, but the way she responded in the second and third sets was impressive.

"She was more aggressive from the back of the courts. In that third set, when it was tight, Rybakina really did show her class."

articles.title: Fans are going crazy for a viral $38 French dip sandwich that is taking over the US Open
articles.summary: Salt Hank's $38 French dip sandwich has US Open fans waiting in half-hour lines for prime rib, provolone, caramelized onions, and au jus dip.
articles.body: Few experiences are as universal as paying an obscene amount of money for food and drinks at a sporting event. I mean, did you even go to a game if you didn't pony up north of $20 for a hot dog and a Pepsi Zero Sugar? Perhaps it's due to widespread cases of the munchies, but fans at the US Open understand this is how it is, and in fact they're embracing it, with huge lines of folks forming for the privilege of scarfing down a $38 sandwich. articles.body:
On Wednesday, Elena Rybakina defeated qualifier Qinwen Zheng in three sets, while Coco Gauff stayed in top form, overcoming 19-year-old wunderkind Mirra Andreeva in a three-set thriller.

Rybakina and Gauff join Aryna Sabalenka and Jessica Pegula in the semifinals—marking the first time the top-four-seeded women all reached the US Open semifinal since 1975.

No. 2 Elena Rybakina def. Qinwen Zheng, 3-6, 6-1, 6-4

No. 4 Coco Gauff def. No. 5 Mirra Andreeva, 2-6, 7-6 (7), 6-2

Coco Gauff outlasted Mirra Andreeva in a three-set thriller to reach the US Open semifinals.

The opening set was less about Andreeva's dominance and more about Gauff's struggle to find her rhythm. The two-time major champion racked up 14 unforced errors and landed only 50 percent of her first serves.

Perhaps most concerning, though, was Gauff's difficulty handling Andreeva's first serve. Despite her reputation as the tour's best returner, Gauff allowed Andreeva to win 13 of 16 first-serve points in the opening set.

Gauff, however, regained her composure and found her rhythm. She steadily eased into the match, using her trademark return skills to force a tiebreak in the second set, which she won.

By the third set, she was in complete control, breaking twice to secure the set and book her place in the semifinals.

In the other quarterfinal match, Elena Rybakina defeated Qinwen Zheng in three sets to reach the US Open semifinal, ensuring that next Monday, she will rise to world No. 1.

Rybakina initially struggled with her first serve and had trouble returning Zheng's strong serve.

However, the two-time major champion quickly found her rhythm in the second set, winning 79 percent of her first-serve points and hitting 10 winners.

In the decisive third set, both players held serve until Rybakina finally broke through late in a game marked by Zheng's errors.

Ultimately, it was another serving masterclass from Rybakina, who won 32 out of 40 points on her first serve.

The semifinals will be played Thursday on ESPN.

Match of the Day: Aryna Sabalenka (1) vs. Jessica Pegula (3)

Aryna Sabalenka stands just two wins away from becoming only the third woman in the Open Era (since 1968) to capture three consecutive US Open titles.

However, Jessica Pegula brings with her not only top form but also vengeance.

Sabalenka has defeated Pegula in back-to-back US Opens, taking the dramatic 2024 final against the American and then beating her again in the 2025 semifinal.

For Pegula to advance, she'll need to continue playing well from the baseline and hit her first serve at a high mark, as Sabalenka is arguably the best second-serve returner on tour, with her ability to put opponents on the defensive end right away.

Pegula is more than capable of winning this match, but considering what's on the line for Sabalenka, it's likely she elevates her play to reach yet another US Open final.

Prediction: No. 1 Aryna Sabalenka def. No. 3 Jessica Pegula in 3 sets

articles.title: US Open: Coco Gauff survives array of unforced errors, double faults while coming back to top Mirra Andreeva in quarters
articles.summary: Gauff rallied from a set down, saved a pair of match points and punched her ticket to the semifinals.
articles.body:
Mirra Andreeva had never beaten Coco Gauff before Wednesday. The 19-year-old Russian was 0-5 against the two-time Grand Slam champion American.

In a US Open showdown between the French Open's past two victors, Andreeva flirted with a long awaited retribution and a chance to inch closer to another major title after asserting her dominance at Roland-Garros in June .

Gauff, though, never went away. As she's wont to do, she battled and dug herself out of hole, embracing the pressure of the moment. On home soil and the hardcourt where she won her first major in 2023, Gauff prevailed.

She endured a head-scratching start and a gut-check second set and won 2-6, 7-6(7), 6-2.

Gauff came into the day firing on all cylinders in a tournament she preceded by winning the Cincinnati Open. She entered Wednesday on a career-long 20-set win streak. Her serve and forehand had been cooperating, leaving her without a real kryptonite in Queens.

Unfortunately for the 22-year-old Gauff, those two aspects of her game faltered in her first set against Andreeva. Her unforced errors piled up early as she dropped the first seven points of the match and quickly went down 2-0. Then her double faulting assisted Andreeva in completing a double break.

Just 12 minutes into the match, Gauff found herself down 4-0. While she scrounged together a couple games down the stretch of that opening stanza, Andreeva stood tall for a 6-2 victory to take a speedy lead at Arthur Ashe Stadium, which had been the site of long, drawn-out competition over the previous 24 hours.

In the first set, Andreeva won 27 points, 11 more than Gauff, whereas Gauff committed 14 unforced errors, nine more than Andreeva. Plus, Gauff wasn't really able to get to net.

But she won four points there to claim a 1-0 advantage in the second set. Just when it looked like she might return to form, she went wide on a forehand at 15-15 in the subsequent game and then on a backhand the very next point.

She lost that game yet kept some scoreboard pressure on Andreeva by winning her second service game of the set. Gauff rebounded from back-to-back double faults with back-to-back effective first serves, including her first ace.

Up 2-1 in the second set, Gauff reached her first break point; however, Andreeva saved it and wound up holding serve to knot things up 2-2.

Still, there's no doubt Gauff was hitting the ball better most of the second frame. And she finally broke Andreeva in the sixth game. The problem was, Andreeva broke back in a marathon seventh once Gauff overhit a backhand and misfired on a forehand.

Both Andreeva and Gauff struggled with their serve late in the set, as they took turns double faulting and breaking each other. In fact, there were four consecutive service breaks. That streak was snapped when Andreeva held to make it 5-5. Although Gauff gutted out a 30-shot rally in a potential set-clinching game, it went to tiebreak.

There, they went back and forth as well.

A Gauff drop shot punctuated an epic 39-shot exchange, giving her a 5-3 advantage in the tiebreak. Andreeva fought back with a signature backhand winner. A long forehand from Gauff drew Andreeva even. Gauff sliced a forehand into the net, setting up a match point for Andreeva. Impossible to count out, Gauff saved that one and another en route to winning the tiebreak 9-7.

Gauff earned a break-point opportunity in the third game of the third set when she tracked down a lob toward the baseline and answered with one over her head. Andreeva volleyed that moon ball into the net, much to the surprise of the crowd.

The next point, Gauff put on a clinic at the net to steal the game. Emotions boiled over for Andreeva, who, until that moment, had maintained her composure. She threw a racket down at the blue acrylic, and it nearly bounced into a cameraman.

From there, Andreeva began to unravel more. Gauff broke her in the seventh game of the final set and served out the match to punch her ticket to the US Open semis.

articles.title: American tennis star Francis Tiafoe praised for ‘classy’ move after US Open win
articles.summary: American tennis superstar Francis Tiafoe pulled off a comeback for the ages in the quarterfinals of the US Open on Tuesday afternoon as he came back and won...
articles.body:
American tennis superstar Francis Tiafoe pulled off a comeback for the ages in the quarterfinals of the US Open on Tuesday afternoon as he came back and won the match while down two sets and a break late in the third set, winning in five sets.

It was a legendary performance from the American star, but it was what he did after the match that led to praise throughout the country.

Tiafoe entered Tuesday's match against fellow American Alex Michelsen as the favorite to win the match, but he found himself in a deep hole, trailing by two sets and a break with Michelsen serving for the match in the third set. Tiafoe ended up breaking Michelsen, winning the game, and then winning the next two sets to take the match.

After clinching the victory, Tiafoe immediately began to celebrate, tossing his racket on the ground. But he instantly cut his celebration short to go console his opponent and friend.

When Tiafoe embraced him, Michelsen immediately began to cry as he was overcome with emotion.

"I really like Alex," Tiafoe said after the match via ESPN . "I really, really do, and I just wanted to come up there and just dap him up. I didn't think it was going to be as long as it was, but I understand the moment. He was definitely crying on my shoulders. Yeah, we just had some words for each other, and that was it."

"I was trying to keep it together and I didn't do a good job of that," Michelsen said. "He was saying a lot of nice personal things. 'You'll be there. When I'm older, you're going to be here, and we're going to play it again in this type of circumstance.' All that good stuff. He's a great guy for consoling me in that moment."

Heading into the match, Michelsen said that Tiafoe is an "unbelievable guy and a very good friend of mine," and he had similar things to say after the match, too.

"I don't think anyone else could have made me cry in that moment, to be honest," Michelsen said.

Needless to say, Tiafoe received a lot of praise for his classy gesture after the match.

"This is why we love Tiafoe. Celebrates, then shares a beautiful moment with his fellow American after an absolute war. Such a class act," wrote broadcaster Tyler Lochte .

"The greatness of sports — and sportsmanship," wrote former ESPN reporter Ed Werder .

"What a match. What a post match hug," wrote Darren Rovell .

"Wants to celebrate, but remembers there were two people on that stage. This is what sports should be," wrote Sean Greene of WDEL.

"Tiafoe is such class act… an amazing story too," wrote former Barack Obama deputy campaign manager Stephanie Cutter.

"The way he delayed/stopped this huge moment of glory to console a friend is such a testament to his character," wrote another fan.

Tiafoe will now face off against fellow American Ben Shelton in the semifinals.

articles.title: US Open Tennis 2026 Top Storylines to Watch in Women's Semifinals Bracket
articles.summary: The top-four seeded women all reached the US Open semifinal for the first time since 1975.
articles.body:
The top-four seeded women all reached the US Open semifinal for the first time since 1975.

On Thursday, two-time reigning champion Aryna Sabalenka will take on top-ranked American Jessica Pegula in a rematch of the 2024 US Open final.

In the other semifinal, No. 2 Elena Rybakina will face No. 4 Coco Gauff.

Below, we've compiled all the key storylines to watch for ahead of Thursday's action.

Aryna Sabalenka faced her toughest challenge yet, overcoming Linda Noskova in a thrilling three-set quarterfinal.

The world No. 1 now stands just two wins away from becoming only the third woman in the Open Era (since 1968) to capture three consecutive US Open titles.

However, Jessica Pegula hopes to end that streak—and claim some revenge.

Sabalenka has defeated Pegula in back-to-back US Opens, taking the dramatic 2024 final against the American and then beating her again in the 2025 semifinal.

Pegula enters this match riding the momentum of her own thrilling victory, having battled back from a slow start to overcome fellow American Emma Navarro.

She has put together an impressive tournament, finding her rhythm at the baseline and excelling with her first serve.

The question remains: does she have enough to upset Sabalenka?

For Pegula to advance, she'll need to limit early unforced errors and establish her first serve quickly.

There's no doubt Pegula can handle the physical demands of this match.

But with so much on the line for Sabalenka, expect her to elevate her game and reach her eighth straight hard court Grand Slam final, tying Monica Seles for the longest such streak by a woman in history.

Next Monday, Elena Rybakina is set to debut as the new world No. 1 on the WTA Tour.

But she most certainly has her eyes set on winning the US Open.

The two-time major champion is seeking to become the sixth woman since 1988 to win both hardcourt majors in the same year.

Rybakina has dominated all tournament long, dropping just one set en route to the semifinal.

The same can be said for Coco Gauff, however.

The 22-year-old American has won 11 consecutive matches, dating back to the Cincinnati Open, dropping just one set in total.

Gauff struggled in the opening set of her quarterfinal encounter before finding her best tennis late to advance past Mirra Andreeva.

Like their previous two encounters, this promises to be another thrilling battle.

Avoiding a slow start like she did against Andreeva will be the most crucial thing for Gauff.

Yes, Gauff is one of the best returners on tour. But, against one of the best servers and baseline players in Rybakina, it'll be more important than ever to find her consistent game early, because service breaks will only come so often.

If she can make the match a physical battle and force Rybakina into extended rallies, this is her golden opportunity to reach the final.

articles.title: US Open 2026 results: Coco Gauff saves match points to beat Mirra Andreeva and set up Elena Rybakina semi-final
articles.summary: Coco Gauff saves two match points to beat Mirra Andreeva and set up a US Open semi-final against incoming world number one Elena Rybakina.
articles.body:
Coco Gauff saved two match points as she fought from a set down to beat Mirra Andreeva and set up a US Open semi-final against incoming world number one Elena Rybakina.

Blown away in a 26-minute opening set, fourth seed Gauff was twice pegged back from a break up in a scrappy second set before coming through a 16-point tie-break to force a decider.

Roared on by a partisan crowd, the American's resilience proved the difference in what became a mental battle as she closed out a 2-6 7-6 (9-7) 6-2 win – a performance she said was inspired by compatriot Frances Tiafoe's comeback victory over Alex Michelsen on Tuesday night.

Progression to the last four marks back-to-back Grand Slam semi-finals for the two-time major champion and her first in New York since winning the title in 2023.

It is the first time the top four seeds have reached the semi-finals of the women's singles at a major since Wimbledon in 2009, after top seed Sabalenka and third seed Jessica Pegula progressed on Tuesday.

"At the end of the first set I was thinking about Frances and how he came back yesterday," Gauff said.

"We all want to do well in front of this crowd. Honestly, I was just trying to leave the court with no regrets."

Gauff also drew strength from her home crowd, something she has learned to embrace having struggled with the pressure of "disappointing" them with a "bad match" earlier in her career.

"I don't have that fear of disappointing them. I'm just using them and knowing that when I step on this court, they're still going to have my back," she said.

Earlier, second seed Rybakina recovered from losing a set for the first time this tournament - and going break-point down in the decider - to beat Zheng Qinwen 3-6 6-1 6-4.

The 27-year arrived at the US Open trailing Aryna Sabalenka by just 434 points and was guaranteed to secure the number one ranking for the first time in her career by reaching the semi-finals.

'Just a number' - Rybakina's rise to world number one

Rybakina reaches #1 as Gauff completes epic semis line-up

This was an uncharacteristic performance from Gauff, whose 22 winners were vastly outnumbered by 42 unforced errors, including 12 double faults.

She won just five of the opening 21 points as Andreeva breezed into a one-set lead and later failed to consolidate breaks at 4-2 and 5-3 in the second set.

A double fault at the beginning of the tie-break felt ominous, but the 22-year-old maintained her composure to save two match points - something which proved a turning point as she dominated the clutch moments in the decider.

Her response was in stark contrast to Andreeva, who struck 14 unforced errors to Gauff's two in the final set and flung a racquet in frustration following the first break of serve.

"You have to admire how Coco does this. She's done it so many times in her career," former British number one Annabel Croft said on BBC Radio 5 Live.

"She's unrecognisable from the player at the start of this match. She was subdued and playing defensive tennis. By the end, she was completely controlling the match.

"We've been blessed with the amount of intriguing matches we've had. You're seeing these warriors out on court.

"It's the ability of one of the gladiators to get themselves back in it."

Addressing her outburst, Andreeva said: "I felt like I was holding my emotions for too long, not reacting on a lot of points. At one point I felt like needed to let it out."

What might have been for resurgent Zheng

Rybakina's ascension to the top of the rankings – the first Kazakhstani man or woman to do so – will rightly dominate the headlines.

She has achieved one of her two goals for the tournament and is now just two wins away from a second major title of the season, having won the Australian Open in January.

However, beaten opponent Zheng's achievements should not go unnoticed, offering a welcome reminder of her talent with an entertaining run to the last eight.

Having dropped out of the top 100 following elbow surgery in July 2025, the reigning Olympic champion navigated three qualifying rounds before registering her first Grand Slam main-draw win since last year's French Open.

She later stunned 22nd seed Madison Keys, who she trailed 5-0 in the third set and saved match point, and eighth seed Iga Swiatek to reach her third quarter-final in New York.

Ranked 121st heading into the tournament, she is now up to 52nd in the live rankings and has just 65 points to defend for the remainder of the season.

But for all the positives, there is an unshakable sense of what might have been against Rybakina.

Momentum was with the 23-year-old after she broke late in the first set before staving off five break points to take a 1-0 lead. However, she was completely blown away in the second set, with her second serve coming under considerable pressure.

She earned a break point in the eighth game of the decider but missed a routine backhand pass. In the next game, she brilliantly fought back from 0-40 to deuce but then followed a loose backhand with a double fault as her hopes of a maiden US Open semi-final slipped away.

articles.title: U.S. Open door is wide open, and an American man must walk through it and win the title
articles.summary: Ben Shelton and Frances Tiafoe meet in the U.S. Open semifinals with Jannik Sinner, Carlos Alcaraz and Novak Djokovic all already eliminated.
articles.body: American men's tennis has run out of excuses. World No. 1 Jannik Sinner withdrew from the U.S. Open prior to the tournament with a knee injury. Then, Novak Djokovic lost in the first round. Finally, in a stunning upset, Ben Shelton sent defending champion Carlos Alcaraz home after a five-set battle that ended at 3:33 a.m. Wednesday morning. BEN SHELTON TAKES DOWN CARLOS ALCARAZ TO EARN THE BIGGEST WIN OF HIS CAREER IN LATEST US OPEN MATCH EVER Now Shelton and Frances Tiafoe will meet in the semifinals on Friday, which guarantees that an American man will play for the U.S. Open championship on Sunday afternoon in Flushing. That's nice, but it isn't enough. One of them needs to hoist the trophy. American men's tennis has run out of moral victories Andy Roddick remains the last American man to win a Grand Slam singles title. He did it at the U.S. Open in 2003, which means the drought is well into its third decade. We've spent more than 20 years searching for the next guy. There have been promising teenagers, big servers, top-10 players and a lot of perfectly respectable runs to the second week of major tournaments. But this is America, and we don't do "respectable." We do dominant. Taylor Fritz reached the U.S. Open final in 2024. Tiafoe made the semifinals in 2022. Shelton got there in 2023. Those are all good runs. But American men have been living off close calls for long enough, and it's time to finish the job. There's arguably never been a better opening for it to happen. The two best men's tennis players in the world aren't standing in the way. Sinner, the No. 1 player in the world and reigning Wimbledon champion, withdrew before the tournament with a right knee injury. Alcaraz, the reigning Australian Open and U.S. Open champ, made it to New York after missing the past two majors with a wrist injury, but Shelton beat him. Djokovic's 39-year-old body betrayed him in a stunning first-round loss to Mariano Navone. Alexander Zverev is still alive, and he finally got over the Grand Slam hump at the French Open earlier this year, in part due to Alcaraz's absence. He's a serious threat, but he's not at the level of either Sinner or Alcaraz, the two players who had combined to win nine straight major titles before Zverev broke through in Paris. The remaining field has good players. It doesn't have an unbeatable one, and sometimes in tennis that's all you can ask for. Ben Shelton and Frances Tiafoe earned this chance Shelton certainly didn't get a free pass into the semifinals. Alcaraz entered their quarterfinal with a 13-0 record against American men in Grand Slam matches. Shelton dropped the first set in a tiebreak, then ripped through the next two to take control of the match. Alcaraz answered with a dominant fourth set, and more than four hours after they started, it came down to a deciding tiebreak. LADIES AT THE US OPEN WERE CAUGHT ON CAMERA TAKING NOTICE OF A SHIRTLESS CARLOS ALCARAZ Despite facing the most pressure-packed moments of his career, Shelton came through to beat the 23-year-old Spaniard. Shelton has had plenty of near misses, which made this victory feel like a breakthrough. The power has never been in doubt. His serve is a weapon, his athleticism jumps off the screen and he feeds off an enthusiastic crowd better than almost anyone on tour. But could he beat one of the sport's giants when the match was on the line and the lights shone their brightest? Finally, that answer is a resounding yes. Tiafoe had to answer a different question. He fell behind fellow American Alex Michelsen by two sets and a break in their quarterfinal and was staring at a quiet exit after squandering a golden opportunity. Things looked especially bleak because Michelsen hadn't dropped a single set in the tournament up to that point. Tiafoe could have folded, especially after all the years of people waiting for him to turn his talent into a major title. Instead, he fought his way back and won in a fifth-set tiebreak. Tiafoe is 28. He's not old, but he's not the young prospect with unlimited time anymore. This is his third trip to a major semifinal, all at the U.S. Open. At some point, the breakthrough has to become more than making it to Friday night. And Tiafoe knows it. "We're going to enjoy this, but we got to keep going," he said after beating Michelsen. Shelton is 23 and probably has more opportunities ahead of him. But ask Dan Marino how many more Super Bowl appearances he thought he'd have after he made his first one at 23. The answer was zero. The American finalist has to finish the job There will be plenty of talk about how great Friday's semifinal is for American tennis, and it is. Arthur Ashe Stadium will be packed and fired up to watch two American stars with big personalities, huge games and a real chance to end a 23-year major-title drought. But the celebration can't peak in the semifinal. We already know an American can reach the final. Fritz did it two years ago, then Sinner beat him in straight sets. Getting another man to the last Sunday would show consistency. Winning could change the sport in this country. That may sound dramatic, but look around. American women's tennis has continued producing major champions. Coco Gauff, Madison Keys and Sofia Kenin have all won Grand Slam singles titles in this decade. The men keep giving fans encouraging signs and asking them to wait a little longer. We can't wait much longer. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Whoever wins between Shelton and Tiafoe will have the New York crowd, a winnable final and the opportunity American men's tennis has spent 23 years trying to create. Sinner, Alcaraz and Djokovic are already gone. The last obstacle will be one very good player on one Sunday afternoon. Many people probably want to already label this tournament as a success because an American man is guaranteed to at least make the final. I'm not one of them. At this point, it's victory or failure. The door is open and it's time to finally walk through it.

articles.title: US Open 2026 results: Alfie Hewett and Gordon Reid into last eight of men's wheelchair singles
articles.summary: British duo Alfie Hewett and Gordon Reid win their respective first-round matches in the men's wheelchair singles at the US Open.
articles.body:
British duo Alfie Hewett and Gordon Reid both reached the men's wheelchair singles quarter-finals at the US Open on Wednesday.

Hewett, the number two seed and a four-time winner in New York, dropped only two games in a 6-0 6-2 victory against Spain's Daniel Caverzaschi and will face American Casey Ratzlaff for a place in the semi-finals.

Reid's match against Frenchman Stephane Houdet was a much closer contest, with the Scot eventually winning 6-3 5-7 6-2 in two hours and 13 minutes.

Up next for Reid is the defending champion and top seed Tokito Oda of Japan, who has won the past six Grand Slam singles titles.

Hewett and Reid are also attempting to win a sixth US Open wheelchair doubles title together as a pairing and won their opening round on Tuesday, with a semi-final against Oda and Argentina's Gustavo Fernandez to come.

Meanwhile, Andy Lapthorne and Greg Slade were beaten in the first round of the quad singles on Wednesday.

Lapthorne lost 6-2 6-1 to top seed Niels Vink of the Netherlands, while Slade was defeated 6-4 6-2 by Gonzalo Lazarte of Argentina.

Lapthorne is still involved in the quad doubles competition and is into the semi-finals alongside South African partner Leon Els.

articles.title: Unseeded Russian Karen Khachanov advances  to US Open semifinals after hobbled No. 28 seed Alexander Blockx retires in third set
articles.summary: Khachanov advances to face the winner of Wednesday's prime-time match between No. 1 seed Alexander Zverev and unseeded Botic Van De Zandschulp.
articles.body:
Alexander Blockx tried to give it a go but the 28th-seeded Belgian was too hobbled to finish Wednesday with a trip to the US Open semifinals at stake at Arthur Ashe Stadium.

Blockx retired in the third set against unseeded Russian Karen Khachanov while trailing 6-2, 7-5, 3-2, unable to continue with a rib injury that had hobbled him since the Round of 16. The injury bothered Blockx throughout the match.

He visibly struggled with his serve in the first set, where he was broken twice. He took a medical timeout between sets to have work done not on his ribs, but his left foot.

He stayed in the match and remained on serve in the second set until Khachanov broke him late to serve for the set, 7-5. Blockx then took another medical timeout, this time to have work done on his torso.

He was in pain in the third set and opted to retire when Khachanov broke him again to take a 3-2 lead. He informed the chair umpire of his decision, then shared an embrace with Khachanov.

Khachanov, 30, advances to face the winner of Wednesday's prime-time match between No. 1 seed Alexander Zverev and unseeded Botic Van De Zandschulp.

Khachanov back in semis despite downturn

The trip to the semifinals marks the second for Khachanov at the US Open. He lost as the No. 27 seed in the semifinals in 2022 to No. 5 seed Casper Ruud, who went on to lose to Carlos Alcaraz in the championship match. It's the third trip to a Grand Slam semifinal and his first since advancing to the Australian Open semis in 2023.

Khachanov willl play in the semifinals ranked 50th in the world, his lowest ranking since 2017. He spoked about the conflicted feelings of defeating an injured opponent in his post-match interview.

"It's a mixed feeling," Khachanov said. "From one side, I was feeling I was dominating from the beginning. Then I started to feel like he was struggling more and more. …

"He's suffering, I don't want to scream 'come on' or something like that. I wanted to keep the energy still there. I wish him a speedy recovery, definitely. … I'm super happy. I'm in the semifinals; come on."

Blockx's run to the quarterfinals was his deepest ever at a Grand Slam and the deepest ever by a Belgian at the US Open. He got there by upsetting No. 5 seed Flavio Cobolli in the third round, then beating No. 24 seed Francisco Cerundolo on Monday in the Round of 16.

He defeated Cerundolo while playing through pain. He told reporters after that match that medication did little to relieve his pain during play.

"I was just hanging in there," he said. "If I would have lost the third set, the chances would have been really high of me retiring."

On Wednesday, the pain alongside a steep deficit to Khachanov proved to be too much to play on.

articles.title: US Open: 3.33am local time and another early-morning finish as Ben Shelton beat Carlos Alcaraz, so does something have to change?
articles.summary: Ben Shelton beat Carlos Alcaraz 6-7 (5-7) 6-1 6-3 1-6 7-6 (10-7) in a match that started just after 11pm and ended at 3:33am Wednesday; watch the US Open live on Sky Sports Tennis and Sky Sports+, streaming service NOW and the Sky Sports app
articles.body:
Three long matches earlier on Tuesday meant Alcaraz and Shelton did not step on to court until gone 11pm .

The US Open craves its night matches and players love the energy the fans provide - even when a number of matches have already gone past 2am this year.

Thousands stayed to the end, with Arthur Ashe Stadium perhaps still one-third full for the finish. Shelton benefited from a home-crowd even against the popular Alcaraz, with fans chanting his name along with "USA! USA!"

"It's incredible," Shelton said. "I always say that this is the greatest sports city in the world, I say that this is the greatest stadium in the world. I'm just hoping that my best friend and my sister over there don't have to be at work at 6am in three hours."

But Martina Navratilova was not impressed at yet another early-morning finish, the former world No 1 posting on X: "Something has got to give - this is not OK and it is not normal - no other sport might start at 11AM or 11PM. In the same event."

So have we now reached an extreme? The early-morning finishes have stirred frustration and concerns about how organisers are managing the schedule at the Grand Slam event with numerous matches straying well past midnight.

The US Open took to social media with a light-hearted nod to the late night, offering a fill-in-the-blank letter for fans to ask their bosses to be excused from work on Wednesday.

"We understand how important showing up is, but sometimes you have to make time for things you're passionate about," the post on X stated. "Carlos Alcaraz and Ben Shelton put on an absolute stellar performance during their US Open quarterfinal, and ______ was a fully committed fan who was completely locked in from start to finish."

Speaking on the Served Podcast, host Andy Roddick defended the late-night finishes, saying: "I know a lot of the comments are, you know, 'How do you finish at 4 in the morning?' and all of that," he said.

"Well, every match goes to a match tie-break except for one. And you've got to get 25,000 people out of a stadium responsibly, and you've got to get 25,000 people in responsibly. So, I hear a lot of complaining. I don't hear a lot of proposed solutions."

What is the impact of late-night finishes?

Sleep schedules, meal times and warm-ups are all impacted by the ticking clock.

"When you finish late, the next day shifts a lot," Aryna Sabalenka said earlier in the tournament. "Like, you still need to get your hours of sleep, so you start later. You just can really mess up your schedule."

Sabalenka is not alone; Venus Williams also said it was "not ideal" that her match against Sofia Kenin last Monday didn't start until past midnight.

"I think it wasn't great for either of us, so I think we both tried our best," she said. "Yeah, I just don't know any other sport where you have to start that late. I definitely think there's room for improvement there."

Speaking on Sky Sports Tennis , coach Ryan Harrison said there's no solution to the late-night finishes while former Wimbledon champion Marion Bartoli concluded: "From a TV point of view it's great because you have people on the edge of their sofa and they want to watch the match from home.

"But I will say, ultimately, one match a night especially when you get down to the quarter-finals and you know those matches are going to be a lot closer could potentially be the solution.

"I'd say in the first week you can have two matches because you know some of the matches might be one-sided, but as you move on, definitely one match."

The US Open is live on Sky Sports from August 30. Stream tennis with no contract on NOW and the Sky Sports App . You can also watch the Laver Cup at The O2 in London from 25-27 September live on Sky Sports.
authors: Raz Mirza at Flushing Meadows, New York

articles.title: Granollers y Zeballos se despiden en los cuartos del US Open
articles.standfirst: La pareja hispano-argentina cedió ante Salisbury y Ram en dos sets
articles.summary: La pareja hispano-argentina cedió ante Salisbury y Ram en dos sets
articles.body: Marcell Granollers, de 40 años, no podrá revalidad el título del US Open en la modalidad por parejas. El barcelonés ha jugado este miércoles diezmado por el esguince de tobillo que se produjo 24 horas antes. Granollers y Zeballos, defensores del título, cedieron en los cuartos ante Joe Salisbury y Rajeev Ram, por 6-4 y 6-4. La pareja hispano-argentina, los segundos cabezas de serie del cuadro, intentó reaccionar a pesar de ir perdiendo por un set y 4-1. Llegaron a situarse 4-3 y 5-4, pero no les dio a nivel físico para repetir en semifinales del Abierto de los Estados Unidos.

articles.title: Andy Roddick claims Ben Shelton has a skill no other tennis player on Earth does after he beats Carlos Alcaraz
articles.summary: Ben Shelton defeated Carlos Alcaraz in the US Open quarter-finals. Delivering arguably the finest performance of his professional career, Shelton beat Alcara...
articles.body:
Ben Shelton defeated Carlos Alcaraz in the US Open quarter-finals.

Delivering arguably the finest performance of his professional career, Shelton beat Alcaraz , 6-7, 6-1, 6-3, 1-6, 7-6.

Shelton aced Alcaraz on match point past 3am on Wednesday morning, advancing to his second career US Open semi-final.

Former US Open champion Andy Roddick has now delivered his verdict on Shelton's performance.

Andy Roddick praises Ben Shelton's lefty-serve after watching him beat Carlos Alcaraz

During the latest episode of ' Quick Served ', Roddick said the following.

"What a big win for Ben Shelton . Finishing up at 3.30am in the morning," he said.

"Listen, Carlos [Alcaraz] coming back after injury and even attempting to win a Grand Slam is otherworldly.

2026 Barcelona Open 1R [WIN] vs Otto Virtanen (148 days ago)

2026 US Open 1R [WIN] vs Roman Safiullin (9 days ago)

2026 US Open 2R [WIN] vs Jaime Faria (6 days ago)

2026 US Open 3R [WIN] vs Wu Yibing (5 days ago)

2026 US Open 4R [WIN] vs Tommy Paul (3 days ago)

2026 US Open QF [LOSS] vs Ben Shelton (1 day ago)

"His forehand was not landing the way it usually does, but Ben saw that and was able to adjust his game plan based on the moment and the Carlos Alcaraz he saw that night.

"He was breaking fantastically well. He returned really well, broke serve more than any of us thought he might in this match, and he did a fantastic job.

Ben Shelton vs Carlos Alcaraz – Match stats

"Even in the fifth set breaker, there wasn't a lot of looking up and saying come on; he kept inward and was disciplined and on message.

"It felt like such a massive growth match for Ben Shelton using that big lefty serve, running it in on his body at 145mph.

"That's a superpower he has which nobody on Earth has.

"I am smiling as I say this, but it sets up an all-American match with Frances Tiafoe."

No American man has won a Grand Slam singles title since Roddick at the 2003 US Open.

And since Roddick retired, only Taylor Fritz (2024 US Open) has played a major final.

However, with Shelton and Frances Tiafoe set for the semis, at least one American will advance to the 2026 US Open men's singles final.

Shelton is the favourite and rightly so.

After all, he did just beat the defending champion and world number three.

The 23-year-old's serve, as Roddick mentioned, is one of the most dangerous weapons in modern tennis.

If he plays like he did against Alcaraz, Tiafoe may not stand a chance.

But if his level dips, his countryman won't hesitate to take advantage…

Ben Shelton rises to provisional career-high ranking

Provided Tiafoe doesn't win the US Open, Shelton will debut at a career-high of fourth on Monday.

And if Shelton wins the US Open, he will close the gap to Alcaraz to within 200 points.

For a player many criticised earlier this year, that's pretty good going.

Shelton's inconsistent form was questioned, playing like a top-five player one week before losing in the first round the next.

This summer, Shelton has established himself as an elite talent.

The American defended his Canadian Open title, and is now back in the US Open semi-finals.

Whether he finishes the job and wins his first Grand Slam or not, Shelton will remember this US Open swing for the rest of his career.

But there is a job to do, and the 23-year-old will be 100% focused on the task at hand.

Shelton will return to play Tiafoe in the semi-finals on Friday, September 11.

articles.title: Rybakina books US Open semi against Gauff, secures No.1 ranking
articles.summary: Elena Rybakina ended Zheng Qinwen's spirited US Open run with a three-set victory on Wednesday, ensuring she'll rise to number one in the world for the first...
articles.body:
Elena Rybakina ended Zheng Qinwen's spirited US Open run with a three-set victory on Wednesday, ensuring she'll rise to number one in the world for the first time.

The 27-year-old Kazakh star beat Zheng 3-6, 6-1, 6-4 and booked a clash with former champion Coco Gauff for a place in the title match.

Men's top seed Alexander Zverev was also gunning for a semi-final spot on Wednesday, taking on Dutch veteran Botic van de Zandschulp.

World number two Rybakina was assured of ending Aryna Sabalenka's reign at number one just by reaching the semis -- even if Sabalenka wins a third straight title.

"It's just a number right now," Rybakina said. "It's a different achievement ... but mostly you think about the titles in the end of the day."

Gauff, who won the first of her two major titles at Flushing Meadows in 2023, saved two match points in a 2-6, 7-6 (9/7), 6-2 victory over Russian 19-year-old Mirra Andreeva, the fifth-ranked reigning French Open champion from Russia.

"Elena is the new world number one," Gauff said. "It's going to be a tough match. These are the moments you live for."

Gauff struggled early, withstood two match points in the tie-break then rallied with some inspiration from Frances Tiafoe's come-from-behind five-set victory over fellow American Alex Michelsen.

"I just had to reset," Gauff said. "Honestly, I was thinking about Frances Tiafoe and how he came back. I was just trying to leave the court without regrets."

In becoming the first Kazakh player to reach number one, Rybakina becomes the 30th woman to reach the top spot. She's chasing a third Grand Slam title after winning the Australian Open in January, four years after winning Wimbledon.

"I feel like you will appreciate and think about it even more when you finish your career," she said of the ranking. "Like now, you still need to keep on going."

Reigning Olympic champion Zheng, 23, missed out on her first US Open semi-final. She lost at the 2024 Australian Open in her only Grand Slam final appearance.

Zheng, a former world number four ranked 121 after missing about eight months due to elbow surgery, went through qualifying and won seven matches in New York, including comeback wins over six-time Grand Slam champion Iga Swiatek and former Australian Open winner Madison Keys.

"I got lot of chances in the third set, but I didn't took it," Zheng said. "That was a bit pity for me to lose this match, but obviously I could take positive things from US Open this year."

Zverev, who claimed his maiden major at the French Open this year, is seeking to return to the US Open semis for the third time -- and his first since 2021.

In van de Zandschulp he could face a trickier proposition than the Dutch player's number 70 ranking implies. Van de Zandschulp famously toppled Carlos Alcaraz in the second round two years ago and sent sixth-seeded Australian Alex de Minaur packing in the second round last week.

He booked his semi-final berth with a five-set win over Arthur Gea, saving a match point against the Frenchman.

The winner of that match will face veteran Karen Khachanov for a place in Sunday's final.

Khachanov advanced when Belgian Alexander Blockx retired from their quarter-final with the Russian leading 6-2, 7-5, 3-2.

"I saw really that he was suffering all over his body," Khachanov said of 21-year-old Blockx, who had already been on the verge of retiring from his fourth-round win over Francisco Cerundolo with a rib injury.

On Wednesday he played with one thigh wrapped and had medical timeouts for treatment on a foot and pain in his lower back.

"I think I finally understand how physical the slams are," Blockx said. "It's totally different from the usual ATP tournaments where it's best-of-three."

articles.title: Khachanov no tiene piedad del lesionado Blockx y pasa por segunda vez a semifinales del US Open
articles.standfirst: El belga se vio obligado a retirarse y el ruso espera al ganador del duelo entre Zverev y Van de Zandschulp
articles.summary: El belga se vio obligado a retirarse y el ruso espera al ganador del duelo entre Zverev y Van de Zandschulp
articles.body: Karen Khachanov, que ya estaba en activo en la época del 'Big Three' de la raqueta, se ha dado una última oportunidad de ganar un título de Grand Slam en el Abierto de los Estados Unidos. Semifinalista en la edición de 2022, su mejor resultado en un major junto a la misma ronda del Open de Australia 2023, dio este miércoles buena cuenta de un lesionado Alexander Blockx, por 6-2, 7-5 y 3-2. El belga se vio obligado a retirarse tras la disputa del quinto juego a la hora y 38 minutos por problemas en la costilla. Ni los antiinflamatorios le permitieron terminar. Khachanov espera en la semifinal del viernes al ganador del duelo de cuartos que mide a Alexander Zverev, primer favorito del cuadro individual masculino, y el neerlandés Botic van de Zandschulp. El moscovita, residente en Dubái, ya avisó de su buen momento de forma cargándose en la segunda ronda a Felix Auger-Aliassime, número cuatro mundial. Karen, que inició el torneo neoyorquino en el puesto 50, asciende 24 posiciones y se sitúa vigésimo sexto, inmediatamente por detrás de su compatriota Andrey Rublev.
